newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Credit Foncier staff to free boss - unions.
newsitem.headline: French Credit Foncier staff to free boss - unions.

text.p: Employees at troubled French bank Credit Foncier will free chairman Jerome Meyssonnier imminently, a spokesman for the trade unions said on Wednesday, the sixth day of a staff siege of the bank's Paris headquarters.
Meyssonnier has been held since Friday by staff opposed to government plans to break up the 145-year-old bank.
"We can expect him to be freed within a few minutes," union spokesman Jean-Claude Mabourde told a meeting of the staff inside the Paris headquarters.

The unions had taken a "wise and reasonable" decision and would now call government-appointed mediator Philippe Rouvillois to further press their campaign to keep the bank, founded by emperor Napoleon III, intact and in business.

Meyssonnier and seven of his colleagues have been held since Friday in the protest over the government plans to break up the group, spin off part of it to another cooperatively run lender called Credit Immobilier and wind the rest down over time.
